text: Provides a typed, extensible agent loop where you can swap the underlying model with a one-line string change
quote: a typed, extensible agent loop with every model a string swap away

text: Same agent object can run behind a web frontend, in a terminal, on a voice call, or on a durable background queue
quote: The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue, or as a plain object you call run() on.

text: Ships a complete coding agent with workspace-rooted file access, allowlisted shell commands, and long-session context management
quote: A complete coding agent in your terminal: workspace-rooted file access, allowlisted shell, repo orientation, planning, and context management that survives long sessions.

text: Agents are generically typed by dependency and output type (e.g. Agent[Foobar, list[str]]) so IDEs catch mismatches
quote: agents are generic in their dependency and output types, e.g., an agent which required dependencies of type Foobar and produced outputs of type list[str] would have type Agent[Foobar, list[str]]

text: Function tools let the model perform actions and fetch extra info to help generate a response
quote: Function tools provide a mechanism for models to perform actions and retrieve extra information to help them generate a response.

text: Can force model output to match a Pydantic model schema for structured output
quote: Here's an example using a Pydantic model as the `output_type`, forcing the model to respond with data matching our specification

text: Exposes the full message history of an agent run, usable to continue a conversation or inspect performance
quote: Pydantic AI provides access to messages exchanged during an agent run. These messages can be used both to continue a coherent conversation, and to understand how an agent performed.

text: Acts as an MCP client, connecting to MCP servers to use their tools during an agent run
quote: Pydantic AI can act as an MCP client, connecting to MCP servers to use their tools as part of an agent run.

text: Supports agent delegation where one agent hands work to another agent and regains control when it finishes
quote: "Agent delegation" refers to the scenario where an agent delegates work to another agent, then takes back control when the delegate agent ... finishes.

text: Durable agents preserve progress across transient API failures, app errors/restarts, and support human-in-the-loop workflows
quote: Pydantic AI allows you to build durable agents that can preserve their progress across transient API failures and application errors or restarts, and handle long-running, asynchronous, and human-in-the-loop workflows

text: Deferred tools support human approval gates and externally-executed tool calls before they run
quote: Pydantic AI provides the concept of deferred tools, which come in two flavors documented below: tools that require approval, tools that are executed externally

text: Built-in support for multiple model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.) out of the box
quote: Pydantic AI is model-agnostic and has built-in support for multiple model providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini

text: Many OpenAI-API-compatible providers can be used via the OpenAIChatModel class
quote: many providers are compatible with the OpenAI API, and can be used with OpenAIChatModel in Pydantic AI

text: Pydantic Evals is a code-first evaluation framework where all components are defined in Python
quote: Pydantic Evals follows a code-first philosophy where all evaluation components are defined in Python.

text: Every agent run generates a trace with spans for each model request and tool call
quote: A trace is generated for the agent run, and spans are emitted for each model request and tool call.

text: Comes with an official CLI ('clai') to chat with LLMs or Pydantic AI agents from the terminal or via a local server
quote: You can use it to chat with various LLMs and quickly get answers, right from the command line, or spin up a uvicorn server to chat with your Pydantic AI agents from your browser.

text: Any Agent instance can launch an interactive CLI session via Agent.to_cli_sync()
quote: you can directly launch CLI mode from an Agent instance using Agent.to_cli_sync().

text: Optional built-in integration with Pydantic Logfire sends detailed agent-run observability data when enabled
quote: Pydantic AI has built-in (but optional) support for Logfire. That means if the logfire package is installed and configured and agent instrumentation is enabled then detailed information about agent runs is sent to Logfire.

text: Instruments surrounding libraries so model calls, tool calls, HTTP requests and DB queries land in one trace, queryable via SQL
quote: Instrument the libraries around an agent to record its model calls, tool calls, HTTP requests and database queries in one trace, then query the result with SQL.

text: Includes TestModel and FunctionModel for testing and developing agents without calling real LLMs
quote: Pydantic AI also comes with TestModel and FunctionModel for testing and development.

text: An agent is conceptually a container for instructions, function tools/toolsets, and a structured output type
quote: conceptually you can think of an agent as a container for: Instructions... Function tool(s) and toolsets... Structured output type

text: Supports programmatic agent hand-off and graph-based control flow as complexity levels beyond simple delegation
quote: There are roughly five levels of complexity when building applications with Pydantic AI: ... Agent delegation ... Programmatic agent hand-off ... Graph based control flow

text: ImageGenerator provides a direct image-generation API (no agent run) supporting OpenAI GPT Image, Google Gemini, and xAI Grok Imagine
quote: The new ImageGenerator gives you a direct API, without an agent run. The same interface supports OpenAI GPT Image, Google Gemini, and xAI Grok Imagine.

text: Can build eval datasets from production traces and compare a candidate agent against a baseline case by case
quote: Evaluate agents and LLM apps against datasets built from production traces, run the suite from your code, and compare a candidate with a baseline case by case.

text: LLM-as-judge scoring keeps the judge's written reasoning and links each verdict back to the trace that produced it
quote: Score answers against criteria you can read. Every verdict keeps the judge's reason and links to the trace that produced it

text: Grades an agent's final output and full tool-call trajectory against datasets, including online evaluation on live production traffic
quote: It grades an agent's final outputs and its trajectory (the sequence and arguments of its tool calls), against datasets in code or, with online evaluation, against a sample of live production traffic.
